title: Go SDK ergonomics: typed structs, generic decode helpers, streaming retry patterns and examples
creator: Amina Patel
description: Improve Go SDK ergonomics for decoding structured outputs into typed Go structs, provide a small set of generic helpers to reduce boilerplate, and add streaming-friendly retry wrappers with clear examples for end users. This ticket covers API surface design, implementation of helpers, unit and integration tests, example apps, and documentation in the SDK repo and docs site.
acceptance_criteria: Provide a concise, well-documented helper package (pkg/decoder) that exposes a small set of generic functions to decode JSON-like model outputs into user-provided typed structs without reflection-heavy overhead.
Streaming decoder utility that supports incremental decode from an io.Reader or a token stream and exposes an ergonomic channel-based iterator for application code.

Retry wrapper for streaming endpoints that can transparently resume where it left off whenever the model/client supports a resumable cursor (or falls back to request-level retries with idempotency keys).
Comprehensive unit tests and two integration examples: (1) simple structured response decode into typed struct, (2) streaming chat assistant with backoff+resume semantics.
Docs and code samples added to the SDK README and example folder; API considered stable for the 2025.03 release and backward-compatible with existing decode helpers where possible.
dev_notes: Prefer lightweight generics (type parameters) for the public helpers instead of reflect-based Unmarshal to keep compile-time type safety and clearer examples.
Keep the streaming API decoupled from transport: accept io.Reader and channel of tokens so it can be used with websocket, HTTP chunked, or custom transports (e.g., dedicated runtime streams).

Retry semantics: two modes — (A) resume-aware: when the service returns a resume cursor, use it to request remaining tokens; (B) best-effort: re-request from start but dedupe by idempotency key and provide caller-visible de-duplication helper.
progress_updates: 2025-02-14: RFC written and reviewed by SDK team. Decided on generics-first approach. See design doc link.

2025-02-20: Prototype of generic Decode[T any](data []byte, out *T) implemented and bench-marked vs json.Unmarshal. Results: roughly equivalent for small payloads; generics wrapper simplifies examples.
2025-02-24: Streaming iterator implemented as StreamDecoder that returns (<-chan T, <-chan error). Initial PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/pull/447
2025-02-27: Added retry wrapper StreamWithRetry(ctx, opts) with exponential backoff and optional resume-token support. Need to reconcile transport-level cursor format with runtime team (ENG-9901).
2025-03-01: Internal review feedback from Mara (platform) to avoid leaking internal cursor formats; changed API to accept an opaque resumeToken string and a TokenSerializer interface.
2025-03-03: Updated examples and fixed race in StreamDecoder close path. Integration test with dedicated runtime flaky on CI; next step: stub streaming transport in tests.
notes_for_reviewers: Focus on public surface: avoid exposing internal resume token shape. Use opaque string and allow runtime to supply a serializer for advanced users.
Benchmarks: include microbenchmarks for Decode[T] vs json.Unmarshal in the PR; check allocations for large structured outputs.
API consistency: keep function names short and idiomatic (Decode, StreamDecode, StreamWithRetry) and place helper pkg under github.com/redwood-inference/go-sdk/decoder.
